title: A Silicon-Proven Unified Low-Latency CXL Controller and Port-Based Routing Switch for Memory-Centric Fabrics
evidence_span: Panmnesia's official ISCA announcement describes a CXL controller that shares buffers across physical, link, and transaction layers to reduce layer-level synchronization overhead, plus a fabric switch supporting port-based routing alongside hierarchy-based routing. The announcement says the design expands memory connectivity while keeping latency in a similar range, improves total bandwidth, and shows stable performance with as many as 64 nodes. It also identifies pre-release PCIe 6.4-CXL 3.2 switch silicon and PCIe 7.0-CXL 4.0 controller IP as productization context.
problem: Early CXL designs inherited PCIe-oriented layer separation and hierarchical connectivity, creating synchronization overhead and limiting the scale of memory-centric fabrics.
method_or_artifact: A unified CXL controller with shared cross-layer buffers and a port-based-routing fabric switch that supports flexible topologies while retaining hierarchy-based routing compatibility.
workload_or_benchmark: Memory-centric CXL fabric scaling and multi-node connectivity; the company announcement reports stable performance with up to 64 nodes but does not expose the full paper’s workload matrix.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Silicon-proven CXL controller and switch, with PCIe/CXL physical interfaces, shared layer buffers, and port-based routing; exact process node, latency, bandwidth, power, and test configuration require the paper.
metrics: stable performance with as many as 64 nodes
similar latency range while expanding memory connectivity
silicon-proven implementation and pre-release product context
limits: The source is an official company announcement, not the captured IEEE paper. It is subject to author/company framing and omits detailed latency distributions, bandwidth numbers, power, area, process, workloads, and independent reproduction.

title: Vistara: Making CXL Real—Full Path from ASIC Design and OS Support to Hyperscale Deployment
evidence_span: The lead author’s ISCA presentation post describes Vistara as Meta’s end-to-end CXL solution spanning ASIC design, firmware, OS-level memory tiering, and hyperscale rollout. It reports deployment across disaggregated ML inference, big-data processing, databases, distributed caches, and software build/test pipelines; the post claims up to 25% fewer servers for disaggregated inference, reuse of decommissioned DIMMs as CXL memory, and tiering overhead below 0.5% in the described production-minded design.
problem: CXL’s usefulness at hyperscale depends on more than an interconnect: ASIC behavior, firmware, OS tiering, tail latency, workload diversity, and deployment operations must work together across production systems.
method_or_artifact: An end-to-end CXL deployment path combining custom ASIC design, firmware, OS memory-management mechanisms, production workload integration, and operational rollout.
workload_or_benchmark: Disaggregated ML inference, big-data processing, databases, distributed caches, and software build/test pipelines in Meta deployment context.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Hyperscale datacenter CXL deployment with custom silicon and OS memory tiering; exact server fleet, CXL generation, workload methodology, tail-latency distributions, and comparison design require the full paper.
baselines: conventional server fleet for disaggregated inference
production tiering alternatives (not fully specified in the post)
metrics: up to 25% fewer servers for disaggregated inference
tiering overhead below 0.5% in the described design
reuse of decommissioned DIMMs as CXL memory
limits: The evidence is a lead-author/company social post, not a full paper or independently audited deployment report. Claims require paper-level verification of fleet scale, baselines, workload methodology, tail latency, overhead definitions, cost, and carbon accounting.
